prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the borehulk. It trundles the deck plate slowly and harms nothing. Its plating is thicker than anything else that walks. Visible features it must show: a colossal mining machine on two broad tracks, a digging tank not an animal; slabs of riveted armour bolted over everything; a heavy boom ending in a conical drill and a bucket scoop slung beneath the front of the hull; a tiny sensor head almost lost on top. One fixed layout in every facing: the working front end carries the boom, drill and bucket; the opposite rear end carries a flat armoured back plate with the engine deck, vents and two exhaust stacks. Chassis proportions are identical in every facing: a broad, long, low hull carried on two wide tracks with a generous gap of hull between them, the track gauge and overall hull width the same whether the machine is seen from the front or from behind. The side view shows the same long hull with the same track width, the boom, drill and bucket projecting from the front end at one side and the exhaust stacks and vents at the rear end at the other. In the rear view the boom, drill and bucket lie on the far side of the hull, pointing away from the viewer and hidden behind the hull, with only the drill tip and the boom elbow peeking over the top edge. The rear view is the side view turned so the exhaust end is nearest the camera. All views share one scale.
